sections.subtitle: Match context
sections.text: Manchester United host Brentford at Old Trafford. The model gives United a small edge (home win 49%, draw 23%, away win 28) and a high chance of both teams to score (63%). United sit 3rd (58 points) while Brentford are 9th (48 points). Expect an open game given both sides’ recent trends.

sections.subtitle: Current form
sections.text: United’s last 5: 2-1-2, with strong attacking moments but defensive swings. They have allowed at least around 1.5 expected goals in 4 of those matches. Brentford are unbeaten in 5 (all draws) and have created 2.0+ expected goals in 3 of those, but finishing and game management have limited wins.

sections.subtitle: Head-to-head
sections.text: Brentford won the last 2 meetings (3-1, 4-3), with both teams scoring in each. Recent head-to-head trends also show the away side have often struck first. Today’s venue change to Old Trafford slightly tilts the balance back towards United.

sections.subtitle: Season stats snapshot
sections.text: United score regularly (58 goals, league rank 3) but keep few clean sheets (6, rank 17). They create many chances (91 big chances, rank 5) but conversion is inconsistent (58 big chances missed). Brentford’s league line reads 48 scored, 44 conceded, with a notable late-scoring profile (76–90 minutes: 16 goals, 32%).

sections.subtitle: Key players and tactical notes
sections.text: Bruno Fernandes leads the league for creativity (18 assists, 109 key passes, 26 big chances created) and remains United’s main supplier. United are dangerous in the air (12 headers scored, rank 2), with Harry Maguire strong in aerial duels. For Brentford, Igor Thiago is in form (21 league goals; 5 in last 5) and is the primary threat, while Ethan Pinnock anchors a resilient back line.

sections.subtitle: Referee, cards and corners
sections.text: Referee Chris Kavanagh averages 3.7 yellows per game (red 0.12). United average 1.61 yellows per game; recent home matches have tended to produce more cards, while Brentford’s recent games have trended lower. Corner profiles point to a moderate-to-high count, with United averaging 4.7 corners per game and both sides’ recent totals often landing around double figures.

sections.subtitle: Match prediction
sections.text: United’s home edge and superior chance creation slightly outweigh Brentford’s unbeaten run. With both teams likely to create clear chances, a narrow United win with both teams to score is the most plausible outcome in line with the model.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match context
halftimeSections.text: Manchester United lead Brentford 2-0 at Old Trafford at half-time. Casemiro opened the scoring with a header on 11', and Benjamin Šeško added a second on 43'. The hosts have been more efficient in the penalty area despite having less of the ball. Headline numbers: possession 46-54, shots on target 5-2, big chances 3-1, expected goals 1.15-0.69, corners 5-5.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Tactical patterns and momentum
halftimeSections.text: Manchester United started fast, pinning Brentford back and threatening repeatedly from crosses and second balls. After the opening goal, the match evened out and Brentford enjoyed their best attacking spell through the middle and into the later stages of the half, forcing United to defend deeper. United then wrestled back control before the interval and converted again. The momentum has swung in phases rather than one-way traffic, but United have been sharper in both boxes.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Key first-half numbers
halftimeSections.text: Manchester United: 3 big chances (1 missed), 5 shots on target, expected goals 1.15, final-third entries 20, penalty area entries 13, duels won 74%, aerials won 80%. Brentford: 2 shots on target, expected goals 0.69, final-third entries 26, penalty area entries 18, duels won 26%, aerials won 20%, 1 big chance missed.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Player highlights
halftimeSections.text: Bruno Fernandes has been United’s main supplier (4 key passes, expected assists 0.59, 1 big chance created). Harry Maguire delivered the assist and added 4 clearances. Casemiro combined a goal with 6 clearances and 2 tackles won. Amad Diallo produced 2 shots on target and missed a big chance. Kobbie Mainoo has been tidy and combative (3 tackles won, expected assists 0.30). For Brentford, Mikkel Damsgaard has offered the most creativity (2 key passes, expected assists 0.40) with Mathias Jensen also contributing progression (expected assists 0.29). Michael Kayode’s close-range chance was the standout miss.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Referee, cards and corners
halftimeSections.text: Yellow cards: Luke Shaw (Manchester United), Sepp van den Berg (Brentford). Corners are level at 5-5, reflecting end-to-end phases. Expect a continued high corner count after the break, with the total likely to finish above 12. With Brentford chasing, anticipate 1-2 additional yellow cards; a red card appears unlikely based on the current game state.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Second-half outlook
halftimeSections.text: Brentford need earlier deliveries and more runners off the ball to turn territorial phases into higher-quality chances. They are losing too many duels and aerials, so variety on the ground and quick combinations around the box will help. United can sit a touch deeper, protect central areas and look to counter through quick outlets, with Bruno Fernandes’ service and Benjamin Šeško’s movement remaining strong routes to goal. Set pieces continue to suit United given their aerial advantage.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match prediction
halftimeSections.text: Manchester United are well placed to manage the lead and strike in transition. The next goal is more likely to fall to the hosts. Predicted full-time score: Manchester United 3-0 Brentford. Expect exactly 1 goal after the break rather than a goal rush.
